summary: Reproduced that GLM-5.3's checkpoint-aware NextN resolver retains modelopt_fp4 but DeepseekModelNextN unconditionally discards it before constructing the decoder. Moved the legacy DeepSeek exception into the base resolver so quantized GLM NextN layers retain FP4 while checkpoint-declared BF16 GLM layers and legacy DeepSeek behavior remain unquantized.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before reproduction: the constructed NextN decoder received quant_config=None for a quantized GLM ModelOpt FP4 checkpoint; the legacy DeepSeek policy was also not represented by the resolver. One independent BF16-ignore boundary passed.

Three passing cases: quantized GLM NextN reaches decoder construction with ModelOpt FP4, checkpoint-declared BF16 GLM NextN resolves to unquantized modules, and legacy DeepSeek ModelOpt FP4 NextN remains unquantized.
Five related NextN unit tests passed, including existing multimodal embedding behavior and the new quantization boundaries.
Changed Python source and regression test compile successfully.

gpu_execution.evidence: rocminfo identifies the assigned GPU as gfx950. The reported checkpoint uses NVIDIA ModelOpt NVFP4 and requires two sm_121 nodes; those weights and that topology were unavailable, so an unrelated AMD smoke was not treated as issue validation.

remaining_limitations: No access to LibertAIDAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 weights in a two-node NVIDIA sm_121 TP=2 environment.
No full server startup, weight-load, generation, semantic-accuracy, or distributed-workload validation was performed.
The open upstream PR https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37322 contains broader generic exclusion-prefix remapping that is outside this issue-specific patch and remains under upstream review.
ruff and black were not installed in the prepared interpreter; git diff --check and compileall succeeded instead.
